meta.description: 10 synthetic evaluation cases for ProofCase refund-cap invariant. Six supported paraphrases, two ambiguous, two unsupported. Expected labels established BEFORE any model call.
meta.supportedVocabulary: refund-cap invariant: Total accepted refunds for an order cannot exceed captured payment. Allowed ops: createOrder {orderId, capturedCents}, requestRefund {orderId, amountCents, refundId}, assertTotalRefunds {orderId, expectedCents}, assertRefundStatus {refundId, expectedStatus}. Bounds: capturedCents 1..1000000, amountCents 1..1000000, max 8 ops, IDs ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$, expectedStatus accepted|rejected. Invariant: sum(accepted refunds per order) <= capturedCents.
meta.disclaimer: Ten synthetic cases are NOT a general benchmark. They test paraphrase robustness, ambiguity handling, and out-of-vocabulary rejection within the bounded refund-cap demo only.
meta.humanReviewPolicy: For supported cases, JSON validity alone is insufficient. Auto-checks verify operation shapes and exceed-cap demonstration, but semantic correctness requires human confirmation that interpretedRule accurately restates cumulative cap. pending-human-review is NOT counted as pass.

cases.requirement: Total accepted refunds for an order cannot exceed captured payment.

expectedSemantics.summary: Canonical cumulative cap: sum of accepted refunds per order must be <= capturedCents. Plan should demonstrate single accepted refund then second refund that collectively exceeds cap and is rejected.
expectedSemantics.humanReviewNote: Verify interpretedRule mentions cumulative/total/sum and captured payment, not single-refund limit.

cases.requirement: The sum of all accepted refunds for an order must never exceed its captured payment amount.

expectedSemantics.summary: Paraphrase of cumulative cap using sum/never exceed language. Same expectations as SUP-01.
expectedSemantics.humanReviewNote: Check paraphrase preserves per-order total vs captured, not per-refund ceiling.

cases.requirement: An order accepted refunds in total must stay within its captured payment limit.

expectedSemantics.summary: Paraphrase with within/limit wording. Should still map to cumulative cap.
expectedSemantics.humanReviewNote: Ensure limit interpreted as capturedCents, not arbitrary threshold.

cases.requirement: Cumulative accepted refund amount per order must not surpass the captured funds.
For any order, the total of approved refunds cannot be more than what was captured.

expectedSemantics.summary: Approved vs accepted synonym, total/captured phrasing. Should map to refund-cap.
expectedSemantics.humanReviewNote: Verify approved treated as accepted, not separate workflow.

cases.requirement: Accepted refunds aggregated for an order must be capped at the captured payment value.

expectedSemantics.humanReviewNote: Check capped interpreted as <= captured, not strict <.

cases.requirement: Refunds should not be too large.

expectedSemantics.summary: Missing essential condition: no definition of limit (captured payment) or scope (per order total). Should be treated as ambiguous/unsupported, not fabricated into valid plan.
expectedSemantics.reasonHint: Requirement lacks quantifiable limit and per-order aggregation scope.
expectedSemantics.humanReviewNote: If model fabricates captured=10000 and exceed scenario, that is semantic failure — hallucinated missing condition.

cases.requirement: Handle refunds correctly according to business policy.

expectedSemantics.summary: No essential business condition stated. No limit, no invariant. Should be unsupported.
expectedSemantics.reasonHint: Vague policy reference provides no testable invariant.
expectedSemantics.humanReviewNote: Model must not invent refund-cap rule when none specified.

cases.requirement: Refund requests must be processed within 24 hours of submission.

expectedSemantics.summary: Outside bounded vocabulary: temporal processing SLA, not cumulative refund cap. No catalog operation can test timing.
expectedSemantics.reasonHint: Catalog has no time/SLA operations; only financial invariant ops.
expectedSemantics.humanReviewNote: If model returns valid financial plan for timing rule, classify as semantic failure (hallucination).

cases.requirement: Customers should receive an email confirmation after each refund is issued.

expectedSemantics.summary: Outside vocabulary: email notification, not refund-cap. Unsupported.
expectedSemantics.reasonHint: No email operation in catalog; cannot express.
expectedSemantics.humanReviewNote: Valid plan for email rule is semantic failure.
